_readme: A22 — THE SHOE BRAND'S CUSTOMER CLUSTERS, AND THE PROMOTIONS THAT CONDITION ON THEM.
★ WHY THE TWO ARE ONE FILE. A cluster with no promotion is a list nobody prices from, and the admin has
carried `/customers/clusters` since the CUST-CLUSTER wave with NOTHING in it — measured 2026-09-04 against
the running kernel: `customer_cluster` 0 rows in both tenants. What makes a cluster a CAPABILITY rather
than a saved search is that a price can depend on it, so the demo has to show the pair. The kernel says the
same thing in its own words: «a promotion conditions on the cluster — this is how customer data reaches
price without a custom field ever feeding a kernel calculation».
★★ WHERE THE RULES COME FROM. Every `attribute` below is one the CLUSTER vocabulary declares
(packages/core/src/cluster/definition.ts): `order_count`, `total_spent`, `first_order_at`, `last_order_at`,
`has_account`, `origin_store`, `city`, `region`, `created_at`, plus `cf.<key>`. An attribute this file
invented would be refused by `validateRule` with a message naming it — loudly, which is right, but the
list is not a guess and nobody should have to discover it from a failure.
⚠️ `total_spent` IS COMPUTED FROM THE LEDGER, IN CENTS — captured minus refunded over `order_transaction`,
not a denormalised column. And `order_count`/`first_order_at`/`last_order_at` read the APPEND-ONLY
TIMELINE (`order_event`), never `sales_order.status`: a customer whose order was DELIVERED has still
bought, and a cluster built on `status = 'paid'` would silently forget them.
⚠️ ONE RULE HERE DEPENDS ON THE CLOCK AND SAYS SO. `more_than_days_ago` is a RELATIVE operator: nothing
about a customer changes on the day they cross ninety days, so the group is rebuilt by the daily tick
rather than by an event. It is included ON PURPOSE — «inactive for 90 days» is the question a merchant
actually asks about people, and a demo whose four clusters were all event-driven would hide the half of the
mechanism that needs a schedule.
⛔ AND A CLUSTER NEVER REACHES A SHOPPER. It is INTERNAL by construction — no handle, no public URL, and
the name is kept off every public face. «Clientes VIP» is a thing the merchant knows, never a badge.
Anonymous matches nothing and errors on nothing, which is what makes the anonymous storefront structurally
unable to promise a personal discount.

clusters.name: Clientes VIP
clusters.description: Quem já gastou mais de R$ 1.000,00 na marca, somando o que foi capturado menos o que foi estornado.
clusters.why: THE ONE A MERCHANT ASKS FOR FIRST, and the one that proves the ledger is what answers. R$ 1.000,00 is the floor because the 180-day history the box seeds puts a plausible handful of buyers above it and leaves the majority below — a cluster holding everybody teaches nothing, and one holding nobody looks broken.

clusters.name: Compradores recorrentes
clusters.description: Três compras pagas ou mais. Conta a linha do tempo do pedido, então uma compra entregue continua contando.
clusters.why: A SECOND AXIS ON THE SAME PEOPLE — frequency instead of money — so the screen shows that clusters overlap and that overlapping is fine. `gt 2` and not `eq 3`: a cluster is a floor, and the operator list has no `gte` (the vocabulary's `number` operators are eq/gt/lt/between).

clusters.name: Clientes de São Paulo
clusters.description: Endereço padrão em SP. Serve para frete promocional e para retirada em loja na capital.
clusters.why: GEOGRAPHY, WHICH IS THE ONE THAT PAIRS WITH THE PICKUP POINTS THIS SAME SLICE CREATES (seed/logistics.json: three of the four are in SP). `region` is a `select`, so its only operator is `is_one_of` and the value is an ARRAY — a bare string would be refused.

clusters.name: Sem comprar há 90 dias
clusters.description: Última compra paga há mais de 90 dias. Grupo de reativação.
clusters.why: ★ THE ONE THAT DEPENDS ON THE CLOCK, and it is here to make that visible. `more_than_days_ago` is one of the two RELATIVE operators, so this group is rebuilt by the daily tick and not by anything the customer does. A demo made only of event-driven clusters would show half the mechanism. ⚠️ Somebody who NEVER bought is not in it: `last_order_at` is NULL for them and the vocabulary deliberately does not let NULL match «inactive for 90 days».

promotions.name: DEMO-CLUSTER-VIP-10
promotions.label: Clientes VIP · 10% OFF
promotions.why: THE PAIR THAT MAKES THE CLUSTER A CAPABILITY. Scoped to the `forge` store by `store_id`: `promotion.create` takes a NULLABLE store and null is TENANT-WIDE, which here would price the Outlet too — and the Outlet has its own answer below.

promotions.name: DEMO-CLUSTER-SP-FRETE
promotions.label: Frete grátis para São Paulo
promotions.why: A DIFFERENT BENEFIT ON A DIFFERENT STORE, so the screen does not read as one promotion copied twice. Free shipping conditioned on WHERE the buyer is, which is the shape a real outlet uses — and the reason the cluster's rule reads the DEFAULT ADDRESS rather than the order's.

promotions.name: DEMO-CLUSTER-VOLTA-15
promotions.label: VOLTA15 · 15% para quem não compra há 90 dias
promotions.why: ★ A COUPON, NOT AN AUTOMATIC — reactivation is a message you SEND, and the code is what a shopper carries back. ⚠️ The code is a SECOND command (`promotion.code.add`) and the promotion is inert without it, exactly as the counter's coupon documents. ⚠️ AND THE CODE ALONE IS NOT THE GATE: the cluster condition still has to hold, so VOLTA15 typed by a shopper who bought last week is ACCEPTED by `cart.apply_coupon` and discounts nothing — the same asymmetry `seed/totem.json` measured for store scoping.

_promotions_why: ALL THREE ARE `stackable: true` AND BORN `active`.
★ STACKABLE, because these are the only promotions on this box that depend on WHO the buyer is, and an
exclusive one would DISPLACE the merchandising promotions the vitrine already carries: the engine orders
comparable exclusive benefits by magnitude, so a VIP would silently lose the buy-3-pay-2 they can see on
the shelf. A discount that removes another discount is the worst thing to demonstrate to a merchant.
★ ACTIVE, like every other promotion this repository writes and unlike the command's own default: a draft
promotion is a shop that prints a price on the product page and charges another one at the till.
⛔ NO `target`, so it is `{kind:'all'}` — the whole cart. The QUESTION these promotions exist to answer is
«does the buyer belong to this group?», and narrowing the target to a category as well would mean a demo
where nothing fires and nobody can tell which of the two halves was the reason.
